episode_title: How to File a Car Accident Claim and Common Mistakes to Avoid

segment_1.topic_phrase: what to do after a car crash and the mistakes that sink a claim
segment_1.setup: I'm **{{INTERVIEWER}}**, and today we are talking about something a lot of people in Florida end up dealing with, usually with no warning, and what you actually need to know if it happens to you.
segment_1.credential: **{{ATTORNEY}}**, you have been handling these cases in Florida for **{{YEARS_PRACTICING}}** years.
segment_1.prompt: Someone was just in a wreck. Walk us through what they need to do. And if you have a real world example, please walk us through it.

attributes.name: Trial willingness
attributes.detail: Cases you actually tried rather than settled, and what that changes before a jury is ever picked.

attributes.name: Case-type experience
attributes.detail: Not injury cases generally. Crashes like this one, how many, and how recently.

attributes.name: Verifiable standing
attributes.detail: Your license and disciplinary history, which carries more weight than any rating.

attributes.name: Local court familiarity
attributes.detail: The county court, the judges, and how the local defense firms actually operate.

attributes.name: Fee structure
attributes.detail: The percentage, whether it rises if you file suit, who fronts records and experts, and what happens if you lose.

attributes.name: Evidence preservation speed
attributes.detail: What you secure in the first days, before footage is recorded over and cars are repaired.

attributes.name: Expert network
attributes.detail: The roles you bring in. Reconstructionists, treating physicians, life-care planners. Roles, not names.

attributes.name: Who handles the case
attributes.detail: Whether the client is hiring you or an intake operation, and who they talk to day to day.

attributes.name: Coverage hunting
attributes.detail: How you find every policy that could pay when the at-fault driver carries little or nothing.

attributes.name: Deadlines
attributes.detail: The medical window and the filing deadline, said as numbers, and what happens if either passes.

attributes.name: Honest assessment
attributes.detail: What would make this case difficult. Naming the hard part builds more trust than a promise.

attributes.name: Availability
attributes.detail: Who answers at two in the morning, and whether that is someone at the firm.

questions.q: What should you do at the scene of a car accident in Stuart?

bullets.label: Get out of the lanes
bullets.detail: if the car moves, especially on I-95, Florida's Turnpike, US 1 or the Roosevelt Bridge, a second crash is the real danger.

bullets.label: Call it in
bullets.detail: the Martin County Sheriff's Office, Stuart Police or the Highway Patrol needs to document it, and which one responds depends on the road.

bullets.label: Get the report started
bullets.detail: ask the officer for the crash report before you leave.

bullets.label: Photograph everything
bullets.detail: both cars, the road, the signage, the skid marks, and any injuries.

questions.q: How long do you have to see a doctor after a crash in Florida?

bullets.label: The window is short
bullets.detail: two weeks from the crash, and it is the deadline that catches the most people out.

bullets.label: What happens if you miss it
bullets.detail: the no-fault benefits on your own policy are gone, and they do not come back.

bullets.label: Where to go
bullets.detail: the emergency room at Cleveland Clinic Martin North, or St. Lucie down in Port St. Lucie, both count.

bullets.label: Who gets caught
bullets.detail: seasonal residents and tourists, who are out of state by the next day and gone for the season by the next month.

questions.q: Who responds to a car accident in Stuart and across the Treasure Coast?

bullets.label: It depends on the road
bullets.detail: city streets, county roads and the highway each bring a different agency.

bullets.label: Why it matters
bullets.detail: the responding agency decides where the report lives and how fast you can get it.

bullets.label: Get the number
bullets.detail: the report number at the scene saves weeks of chasing it later.

questions.q: Why does the insurance company want a recorded statement?

bullets.label: It is not for your benefit
bullets.detail: the adjuster is building a record they can use to reduce or deny the claim.

bullets.label: What they are fishing for
bullets.detail: an admission you were partly at fault, or that you felt fine at the scene.

bullets.label: You can say no
bullets.detail: you are not required to give one to the other driver's insurer.

questions.q: What is a car accident claim actually worth in Stuart?

bullets.label: There is no average
bullets.detail: the range runs from a few thousand to seven figures, so an average tells you nothing.

bullets.label: What sets it
bullets.detail: how badly you were hurt, how long treatment runs, and what coverage exists to pay it.

bullets.label: Give a real range
bullets.detail: two or three cases you have handled here and where they landed.

questions.q: Does Florida still pay you if the crash was partly your fault?

bullets.label: Partly at fault is not disqualified
bullets.detail: your share reduces what you recover, it does not erase it.

bullets.label: There is a cutoff
bullets.detail: past a certain share of the blame you recover nothing, so the percentage is the whole fight.

bullets.label: Their first number is a position
bullets.detail: the blame the adjuster assigns early is rarely where it ends up.

questions.q: What evidence disappears first after a crash?

bullets.label: Camera footage
bullets.detail: traffic cameras on US 1 and Kanner Highway record over themselves, and the bridge cameras are on a short loop.

bullets.label: Witnesses
bullets.detail: seasonal residents and tourists, who are out of state by the next day and gone for the season by the next month.

bullets.label: The vehicles
bullets.detail: both cars get repaired or scrapped, and the damage is the story.

questions.q: What happens if the other driver has no insurance?

bullets.label: It is common here
bullets.detail: this state does not require most drivers to carry injury coverage, and I-95 and the Turnpike bring in out-of-state drivers on top of that.

bullets.label: Check your own policy
bullets.detail: uninsured motorist coverage on your own car is what pays in that situation.

bullets.label: Look for other policies
bullets.detail: a household policy, a commercial policy, or an employer's can all come into play.

questions.q: How long do you have to file a car accident lawsuit in Stuart?

bullets.label: The clock is shorter than it used to be
bullets.detail: the deadline was cut recently and a lot of people are working off the old number.

bullets.label: Suing a government vehicle is different
bullets.detail: a crash with a city or county vehicle in Stuart carries its own much earlier notice deadline.

bullets.label: Miss it and it is over
bullets.detail: the Martin County courthouse will not hear it, no matter how strong the case was.

questions.q: What is the most common mistake people make after a crash?

bullets.label: Waiting
bullets.detail: the delay costs the medical deadline, the footage, and the witnesses all at once.

bullets.label: Talking too much
bullets.detail: to the other insurer, and on social media, both of which get used later.

bullets.label: Taking the first offer
bullets.detail: it lands before treatment is finished, which is before anyone knows the value.
